chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Taymuli, from Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad Al-Halabi, from his father, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Sa'ee between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa has been made to humble the tyrants.

key_terms.السَّعْيُ: The ritual walking between Safa and Marwa
key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa, one of the two hills in Mecca
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwa, the second hill in Mecca
key_terms.لِلْجَبَّارِينَ: For the tyrants or arrogant ones

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual wisdom behind the Sa'ee ritual in Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the metaphysical wisdom behind the Sa'ee ritual, describing it as a manifestation of 'humiliation for the tyrants' (mazzallatan lil-jabbarin). This signifies that the physical exertion of the pilgrims serves to diminish the pride of those who claim absolute authority, reminding them that true sovereignty belongs to Allah. In Shia exegesis, this act transforms a pre-Islamic tradition into a spiritual victory over worldly arrogance.
